title: 観世流謡本 (Kanze-ryū Utaibon), Vol. 11a
shelf_note: A Kanze-school chanting book in cursive with red and black vocal notation; the sampled pages are from Tsunemasa (経政), Kochō (胡蝶) and Torioibune (鳥追舟). It belongs on a Japanese shelf.
structure_note: There are 152 page records against pages_count 102 (and 144 vs 96 translated), so the count field and the records disagree, which may be a re-split or re-import. Only 5 pages carry a printed number, so the 2 backsteps and 1 repeat are probably misread folio numerals, not a real reordering.

book_verdict: The right images and a fair-to-good kuzushiji transcription of three plays, but the English is not a translation on any of the four pages: speaker labels become nonsense words and the key lines (Tsunemasa's ghost, Zhuangzi's dream, the threat to the children) are invented over.
reader_summary: This is an Edo-period Kanze chanting book; the sampled pages come from Tsunemasa, Kochō and Torioibune. The Japanese transcription follows the cursive text closely, apart from notation marks read as digits and a few misread kana. The English cannot be trusted: on every sampled page it replaces the play's lines with invented phrases.

book_verdict: The images are right and the cursive transcription is mostly good, but the English invents or reverses the central lines of Yorimasa, Hachi no ki and Hagoromo and mistranslates Byōdō-in as 'Heike-in'.
reader_summary: This is an Edo-period Kanze chanting book holding Yorimasa, Hachi no ki and Hagoromo. The Japanese transcription is usable, with some misread kana and dates invented from notation marks. The English cannot be trusted: famous passages are dropped, reversed or replaced, and Byōdō-in becomes 'Heike-in'.

title: 観世流改訂謡本 (Kanze-ryū Noh Texts)

book_verdict: The right images of a revised Tamura, but the cursive transcription invents or misreads place names and whole clauses (Nagato, Hōshō-bō, and the cherry-blossom passage on p.15), and the English faithfully carries those inventions.
reader_summary: This is a revised Kanze chanting book of the play Tamura, set at Kiyomizu temple. The transcription is the right text but with serious misreadings: several clauses and place names are replaced by plausible inventions, and the notation is stuffed into the text as tags. The English follows that flawed transcription, so it cannot be trusted line by line.

title: Genji Monogatari Ekotoba (源氏物語絵詞), Vol. 1
shelf_note: An illustrated Genji handscroll at the National Diet Library (target label: 『源氏物語絵巻』 請求記号 ん-98).
structure_note: 19 records for 19 frames, consistent. The catalogue is wrong: 'published 1100' and the title 'Ekotoba' do not match the object. NDL labels it 源氏物語絵巻 ん-98, and the painting style and the Meiji/Taishō accession stamps point to a later copy, not a Heian original (I7).

book_verdict: A fine NDL Genji handscroll with a largely correct transcription, but the English on every sampled page is unrelated to the Japanese, including the Azumaya poem, and the catalogue gives a Heian date to what the holding library labels a later 絵巻.
reader_summary: This is an illustrated Genji handscroll from the National Diet Library (label ん-98), catalogued with an impossible date of 1100. The cursive text is transcribed reasonably well, and the painting descriptions are accurate. The English does not translate the text on any sampled page, so show the images and the transcription only, not the translation.
